experiment: ERA on AgentDescent -- SWE-bench Science, one tree per task
protocol: ERA's, not the benchmark's: the leaderboard gives an agent one attempt per task with no verifier feedback, while this scores a tree of agent sessions against the visible part of each private suite and keeps the best node. `benchmark_reward_*` is the release's own grader over the whole private suite; the search never reads it.

index 394c839..e9d6898 100644
--- a/source/Bio/SeqFeature.py
+++ b/source/Bio/SeqFeature.py
@@ -1710,10 +1710,22 @@ class CompoundLocation(Location):
         versions of Biopython which would have given join{[5:29](-), [37:52](-)}
         and the translation would have wrongly been "EXAMPLE*SILLY" instead.
 
+        This part ordering is only correct when the parts carry an explicit
+        (possibly mixed) strand, since the strand then fixes the biological
+        5' to 3' reading direction of each part independently of the parent's
+        coordinate frame. When none of the parts have a defined strand there
+        is no such reading direction to preserve - the compound location is
+        simply an ordered concatenation of physical regions of the parent
+        sequence, and reversing the parent reverses that concatenation too
+        (mirroring how a single strand-less SimpleLocation is flipped). In
+        that case the part order must be reversed so that extracting the
+        flipped location from the flipped sequence still yields the same
+        biological content (the reverse complement of the original extract).
         """
-        return CompoundLocation(
-            [loc._flip(length) for loc in self.parts], self.operator
-        )
+        flipped_parts = [loc._flip(length) for loc in self.parts]
+        if all(loc.strand is None for loc in self.parts):
+            flipped_parts.reverse()
+        return CompoundLocation(flipped_parts, self.operator)
 
     @property
     def start(self):

index c3dc5b2..73072f8 100644
--- a/source/xgcm/padding.py
+++ b/source/xgcm/padding.py
@@ -105,7 +105,9 @@ def _pad_face_connections(
     # Detect all the axes we have to deal with during padding
     # all the axes defined in the connections + the axes of the padding width should give all axes we need to iterate over
     pad_axes = list(
-        set(_get_all_connection_axes(connections, facedim) + list(padding_width.keys()))
+        dict.fromkeys(
+            _get_all_connection_axes(connections, facedim) + list(padding_width.keys())
+        )
     )
 
     padding_width = {axname: padding_width.get(axname, (0, 0)) for axname in pad_axes}
@@ -153,6 +155,17 @@ def _pad_face_connections(
     n_facedim = len(da[facedim])
     faces = []
 
+    # The dimension order of a single face slice (excluding facedim) that we must
+    # preserve. Concatenating a squeezed (dimensionless-in-the-concat-axis) source
+    # slice against a target slice lets xarray's automatic dimension broadcasting
+    # decide where the reconstituted axis goes, and that placement depends on
+    # which axis we process first (which, prior to this fix, was itself
+    # nondeterministic due to iterating over a `set` of axis names). Restoring the
+    # original per-face dimension order after each face is fully padded keeps the
+    # result deterministic and consistent with the input layout regardless of the
+    # order axes were processed in.
+    face_dims = tuple(d for d in da.dims if d != facedim)
+
     # Iterate over each face and pad accordingly
     for i in range(n_facedim):
         target_da = da_prepadded.isel({facedim: i})
@@ -296,6 +309,7 @@ def _pad_face_connections(
                             join="override",
                         )
                         # TODO: Can we do this with an assignment in xarray? Maybe not important yet.
+        target_da = target_da.transpose(*face_dims)
         faces.append(target_da)
 
     da_padded = xr.concat(faces, dim=facedim)
